**Yes, the cable can limit charging speed.** Charging runs at the lowest of what the charger, the cable, and the device each support. USB-IF notes that a certified cable doesn't add to the capabilities of the products it connects ([USB-IF](https://www.usb.org/cable_connector)).

## What the tiers mean

- **60W cable:** carries 20V at 3A ([USB-IF](https://www.usb.org/cable_connector)). It's fine for phones, tablets, and many laptops, but it caps you at 60W even on a stronger charger.
- **100W cable:** carries 20V at 5A. The cable's e-marker chip tells the charger it can safely handle that current ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/answers/usb-c-cable-60w-100w-240w-charging-speed-e-marker-usb-if-official)). USB-IF stopped certifying 100W USB-C cables on December 22, 2021. Certified cables are now only 60W or 240W ([UL Solutions](https://www.ul.com/insights/240w-usb-c-cable-performance-testing-and-safety-considerations)). 100W cables are still sold, but they predate the current labeling.
- **240W (EPR) cable:** carries 48V at 5A and must have an e-marker. The higher voltage steps are 28V for 140W, 36V for 180W, and 48V for 240W ([USB-IF](https://www.usb.org/usb-charger-pd)).

## How to pick

- **Phone, tablet, or a laptop under 60W:** a 60W cable is enough.
- **Laptop charging at 65-100W:** get a 5A, e-marked cable (100W or 240W).
- **Gaming laptop or other 140-240W device:** you need a 240W-rated cable, plus a charger and device that support that power.
- **Look for the printed wattage logo** (60W or 240W). USB-IF requires it on every certified USB-C to USB-C cable ([USB-IF](https://www.usb.org/cable_connector)).

## One 100W option

The [Baseus USB-C to USB-C Cable, 100W](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-usb-c-cable-100w) is rated 100W (5A, e-marked) and costs $9.99 for 1 m, $12.99 for 2 m, and $16.99 for 3 m ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/answers/usb-c-cable-60w-100w-240w-charging-speed-e-marker-usb-if-official)). It suits a 65-100W laptop charger, but there are some caveats:

- It isn't rated for 140W or 240W.
- Data is USB 2.0 only (480 Mbps), with no video output, so it's a charging cable.
- Baseus says it doesn't support iPad Pro charging.
- The listing doesn't say whether it's USB-IF certified, so I can't confirm that.

That link is an affiliate link, so Dealectric is paid if you buy, at no cost to you. I only have data on this one cable, so I can't compare it with 60W or 240W options. For a certified cable, you can search USB-IF's [product list](https://www.usb.org/products).

If you tell me what device and charger you're using, I can say which tier you need.
